Boston Celtics' 9.3% reflects their solid 56-26 East mark and second-place finish despite recent stumbles, while East contenders like Knicks (4.7%) and Cavaliers (4.2%) trail due to the West's superior depth and OKC's repeat momentum entering conference semifinals.

title: LoL: Weibo Gaming vs Invictus Gaming (BO3) - LPL Group Ascend
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between Weibo Gaming and Invictus Gaming in the LPL Group Ascend, initially scheduled for May 1 at 7:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Weibo Gaming" if Weibo Gaming win the match against Invictus Gaming.

This market will resolve to "Invictus Gaming" if Invictus Gaming win the match against Weibo Gaming.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: In LPL 2026 Split 2 Group Ascend double round robin, mid-table Weibo Gaming and Invictus Gaming clash in a pivotal BO3 rematch after WBG's 2-1 win over IG on April 15. WBG enters with momentum from a 2-0 upset over second-place Top Esports three days ago, boosting their 3-6 series record amid Hang's integration post-Tian departure, while struggling against top teams like Bilibili Gaming. IG, sitting 3-5 after a 0-2 loss to surging Anyone's Legend, leverages offseason additions Breathe, JiaQi, and Fury for stylistic edges in the current patch meta favoring aggressive junglers. Head-to-head splits evenly at 11-9 WBG, with playoff positioning on the line for top-four direct qualification in this closely contested group stage matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: Orlando Magic hold a 3-2 series lead over the top-seeded Detroit Pistons in the Eastern Conference first-round playoffs, with Game 6 set for May 1 at Kia Center, giving Orlando home-court advantage in a potential closeout. Franz Wagner's confirmed absence due to a right calf strain from Game 4 significantly hampers Magic's scoring and spacing, as seen in their Game 5 loss 116-109 where Paolo Banchero posted 45 points. Detroit's Cade Cunningham exploded for 45 points in that win, fueling momentum, though Tobias Harris (ankle) and Kevin Huerter (adductor) are questionable per latest injury reports. Pistons dominated regular season at 60-22 versus Magic's 45-37, but Orlando's paint dominance and rebounding edge in prior wins keep the matchup competitive.

title: Counter-Strike: G2 vs FaZe (BO3) - BLAST Rivals Playoffs
description:

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

This market will resolve to "Even" if the total combined rounds played by both teams in Map 3 is an even number.

"Total combined rounds" is the sum of rounds won by both teams during the match, including any overtime rounds if applicable. For example, a match ending 13–11 would have a total of 24 rounds (even), while a match ending 13–10 would have a total of 23 rounds (odd).

If Map 3 is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Map 3 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Map 3 is not played because the series result has already been determined (e.g., a team clinches the series before Map 3 is needed), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Map 3 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. However, if https://hltv.org has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead.

markets.question: Map Handicap: FaZe (-1.5) vs G2 (+1.5)
markets.description:
This market refers to the Counter-Strike Quarterfinal 1 match between G2 and FaZe in the BLAST Rivals Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 1 at 3:30PM ET.

This market will resolve to "FaZe" if FaZe wins 2 or more maps than G2 in this match.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "G2". 

Maps won by forfeit, disqualification, walkover, or default are counted towards the handicap, provided that the match is completed.

If the match is canceled (not played at all for any reason), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's match forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match ends due to the clinching map being forfeited this will count as a completed match.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. However, if https://hltv.org has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a modest 38% chance of a US-Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026, reflecting stalled diplomacy despite recent Iranian proposals. Following a Pakistan-mediated two-week ceasefire on April 8 amid the 2026 Iran war—sparked by US-Israeli strikes on February 28—negotiations in Islamabad have faltered over Iran's nuclear program, ballistic missiles, sanctions relief, and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer yesterday, vowing to maintain the US naval blockade, while Iran insists on phased concessions; no second round is scheduled, though White House statements signal interest in a lasting agreement ending hostilities. Escalation risks persist absent breakthroughs.

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $150 in May?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil front-month futures settled near $102 per barrel on May 1, paring weekly gains amid trader hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire easing Strait of Hormuz supply risks that propelled first-quarter prices sharply higher on military escalations. Backwardation in the curve signals tight near-term physical supply, with US inventories at 459.5 million barrels—1% above five-year averages—following a 913,000-barrel draw in the prior week. Softening global demand growth forecasts of 0.6 million b/d for 2026 per EIA, coupled with non-OPEC production gains, cap upside, while EIA expects Brent to peak at $115/bbl in Q2. Key catalysts include tomorrow's EIA inventory report and OPEC/IEA monthly outlooks on May 13.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the Lakers holding a 3-2 lead in this Western Conference first-round playoff series, Game 6 at Houston's Toyota Center pits a desperate Rockets squad against a turnover-plagued Los Angeles team desperate to advance. The Rockets, down 3-0 after Lakers wins in Games 1-3, rallied with victories in Games 4 (115-96) and 5 (99-93), capitalizing on LA's 15 turnovers in the latter for 18 points while their young core—Reed Sheppard, Amen Thompson, Jabari Smith Jr., Tari Eason, and Alperen Sengun—forced the issue without Kevin Durant (left ankle sprain, out). Lakers star Luka Dončić remains sidelined (hamstring), though Austin Reaves returned from a four-week oblique absence in Game 5 but shot inefficiently off the bench; LeBron James' availability anchors LA amid road challenges and ball-security woes. Trader consensus reflects a tight matchup shaped by these injury-depleted rosters and Houston's home-court momentum.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

If at any point it is impossible for the listed candidate to win Eurovision 2026 based on the rules of the competition (i.e. they are eliminated), this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's duo Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen lead Polymarket's trader consensus at 34% implied probability for the Eurovision 2026 win in Vienna, driven by their national final triumph with the violin-infused pop anthem "Liekinheitin" and dominance in bookmakers, fan polls, and Eurojury rankings, signaling broad jury and televote appeal amid praised live chemistry from pre-parties. Greece's Akylas follows at 17% with "Ferto," an edgy, original track gaining jury momentum from strong precursor performances and OGAE votes, positioning it as a potential televote dark horse in a Balkan-leaning field. Denmark's Søren Torpegaard Lund holds third at 13% on "Før vi går hjem"'s heartfelt balladry, though pre-party critiques tempered top-tier hype. Australia and France tie at 7%, buoyed by jury-friendly staging previews. First rehearsals begin today, a pivotal catalyst before semis on May 12/14 and final on May 16, where production polish could upend this wide-open contest.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads Polymarket trader consensus for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination at 26.4% implied probability, driven by March-April 2026 California polls showing him trouncing Kamala Harris by double digits in their home-state primary matchup, alongside his national book tour in early primary states like New Hampshire and sustained anti-Trump messaging that bolsters fundraising and visibility. Harris at 11.5% faces 2024 campaign baggage despite some national polls giving her an edge, while Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's 8.5% reflects progressive youth appeal and Jon Ossoff's 6.6% surge ties to Georgia incumbency strength. The wide-open field could consolidate behind 2026 midterm standouts in swing states, governors with executive records, or those securing party endorsements ahead of primaries.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. at 49% implied probability to secure the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, propelled by his high-profile role as HHS Secretary and the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement's growing traction among GOP voters ahead of 2026 midterms, highlighted by his April 22 Senate Health Committee testimony exposing pharmaceutical influences. Vice President J.D. Vance holds steady at 38.6% as the presumed post-Trump successor, bolstered by topping the March CPAC straw poll despite some donor shifts, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio climbs to 20.6% on foreign policy gains. Term limits bar President Trump's third run, opening a contested primary; 2026 midterm outcomes could reshape early frontrunner dynamics.

title: Fed Decision in June?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's June 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their June meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Polymarket traders price a 95.5% implied probability of no change in the federal funds rate at the June 16-17, 2026 FOMC meeting, reflecting strong consensus after the Federal Reserve's April 29 decision to hold rates steady amid sticky inflation and resilient labor conditions. March CPI rose 3.3% year-over-year—above the Fed's 2% target—while nonfarm payrolls added 178,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.3%, signaling no urgency for cuts or hikes. Powell's final press conference as chair emphasized balanced risks, with futures markets implying a steady path near 3.6%. Realistic challenges include softer April CPI data due May 12 or weakening job reports, potentially reviving cut odds above 4%.

title: LoL: Top Esports vs Anyone's Legend (BO3) - LPL Group Ascend
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between Top Esports and Anyone's Legend in the LPL Group Ascend, initially scheduled for May 1 at 5:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Top Esports" if Top Esports win the match against Anyone's Legend.

This market will resolve to "Anyone's Legend" if Anyone's Legend win the match against Top Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

markets.question: Game 1: Both Teams Slay Baron Nashor?
markets.description:
This market is about whether both teams slay the Baron Nashor at least once during Game 1. Baron Nashor is a powerful neutral objective in League of Legends that first spawns at 20:00 game time and respawns 6 minutes after each death, granting the slaying team the Hand of Baron buff.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Top Esports and Anyone's Legend each slay Baron Nashor at least once during Game 1. This market will resolve to "No" if either team (or both teams) does not slay Baron Nashor during Game 1.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is not played because the series result has already been determined (e.g., a team clinches the series before Game 1 is needed), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 begins but is not completed and ends via surrender, this market will resolve based on whether both teams had slain Baron Nashor prior to stoppage. If the condition was not met, this market will resolve to "No".

If Game 1 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

markets.question: Game 1: Both Teams Slay a Dragon?
markets.description:

This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Top Esports and Anyone's Legend each slay at least one elemental dragon during Game 1. This market will resolve to "No" if either team (or both teams) does not slay any elemental dragon during Game 1. Only elemental dragons count toward this market — Elder Dragon kills do not count.

eventMetadata.context_description: Top Esports and Anyone's Legend meet in a pivotal LPL 2026 Split 2 Group Ascend BO3 rematch, both holding 6-3 records with TES second on game differential (+6) ahead of AL's third-place surge (+5) on a four-win streak. TES dominated their Week 1 clash 2-0 but stumbled recently with back-to-back losses to Weibo Gaming, snapping an earlier sweep streak against BLG, JDG, and others bolstered by new top laner ZUIAN and jungler Tian. AL counters with momentum from wins over Invictus Gaming and Ninjas in Pyjamas, powered by jungler Tarzan's MVP performances amid Fearless Draft format. Top-four positioning in double round-robin stakes direct Knockout Stage qualification.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers hold a 3-2 series lead over the Toronto Raptors heading into Game 6 on Friday at Scotiabank Arena, positioning them one win from advancing in the NBA playoffs first round. The Raptors face mounting injury challenges, with Brandon Ingram ruled out due to right heel inflammation after exiting Game 5 early and Immanuel Quickley sidelined for the series with a hamstring strain, thinning their backcourt and scoring options. Cleveland enters with a clean injury report, bolstered by Evan Mobley's dominant second-half performance (23 points) in their 125-120 Game 5 road victory that erased a halftime deficit. Scottie Barnes remains available despite a quad contusion, anchoring Toronto's two-way play, while Donovan Mitchell's scoring and home-road resilience factor heavily in trader consensus amid the Raptors' must-win desperation.

title: Elon Musk # tweets April 28 - May 5, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from April 28 12:00 PM ET to May 5, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the listed driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2026 F1 season.

This market will resolve as soon as the official results of the final scheduled race of the 2026 F1 season are known.

If multiple drivers tie for first place in the drivers standings, this market will resolve according to the tiebreak procedure used by F1 to determine the 2026 F1 Drivers’ champion.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2026 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes teammates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominate early trader consensus for the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship, with Antonelli's back-to-back Grand Prix wins in China and Japan propelling him to 72 points and a slim nine-point lead over Russell's 63 after his Australia victory. This intra-team rivalry on the superior Mercedes machinery—bolstered by strong qualifying head-to-heads and consistent podiums—fuels the razor-thin 30.7% vs. 30.5% implied probabilities, underscoring high uncertainty in a 24-race season amid rivals' struggles, like Charles Leclerc's distant third at 49 points for Ferrari. Miami GP practice hints at further upgrades, keeping the title fight fiercely competitive.

eventMetadata.context_description: Zac Gallen (3.14 ERA, 1-1) takes the mound for the Arizona Diamondbacks against Chicago Cubs righty Colin Rea (4.61 ERA, 3-1) in Friday's series opener at Wrigley Field, where the Cubs (19-12) hold a slight edge over the visiting D-backs (16-14) atop the NL Central race. Gallen's ace credentials and recent injury scare clearance tilt the pitching matchup toward Arizona, while Chicago's staff grapples with ongoing ailments including Justin Steele's setback and a thin bullpen. D-backs catcher Gabriel Moreno returns from the injured list boosting their lineup, but Cubs 2B Nico Hoerner exited early amid injury concerns; overcast skies and northeast winds favor pitchers in this early-season clash with playoff implications looming.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance commands trader consensus at the top of 2028 presidential odds, buoyed by his incumbency advantage, recent high-profile fundraising with major Republican donors, and sharp America First rhetoric on immigration and tariffs that resonates in battleground states. California Governor Gavin Newsom trails closely as the leading Democrat, though his odds have softened amid party introspection following 2024 and sidestepped 2028 talk tied to family and 2026 midterm priorities. Secretary of State Marco Rubio sits third after a March surge linked to his cabinet role and CPAC straw poll strength, but lacks recent momentum. This tight race reflects pre-primary uncertainty, with 2026 midterms poised to elevate performers in swing states or expose vulnerabilities, potentially widening gaps via party nominations or Trump endorsements.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 94.5% for Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by May 15, reflecting persistent disruption from the U.S. naval blockade imposed amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict that began in March 2026. Shipping data shows transits at a trickle—only six vessels in the past 24 hours versus pre-war hundreds—after U.S. forces turned back six Iranian oil tankers last week and enforced restrictions, stranding over 2,000 ships and 20,000 sailors in the Gulf. Iran has threatened "long and painful strikes" on U.S. positions if attacks resume, while peace talks remain stalled with no deal in sight. Brief reopenings, like on April 21, quickly reverted amid ceasefire breakdowns involving Israel, underscoring significant barriers to normalization absent a major diplomatic breakthrough.

title: Sabres vs. Bruins
description:
In the upcoming NHL game, scheduled for May 1 at 7:30PM ET:
If the Sabres win, the market will resolve to "Sabres".
If the Bruins win, the market will resolve to "Bruins".
If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed.
If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50-50.
The result will be determined based on the final score including any overtime periods and shootouts. In the event of a shootout, one goal will be added to the winning team's score for the purpose of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Buffalo Sabres hold a 3-2 series lead over the Boston Bruins entering Game 6 of their Eastern Conference First Round Stanley Cup Playoffs matchup at TD Garden, where a win advances the top-seeded Atlantic Division Sabres. Recent injury developments shape lineups: Sabres rookie forward Noah Ostlund is out with a lower-body injury from Game 5's overtime loss, but Josh Norris returns on a line with Josh Doan and Zach Benson after missing three games; defenseman Logan Stanley is a game-time decision with illness. Bruins forward Viktor Arvidsson remains sidelined by an upper-body issue for a second straight contest. Alex Lyon is set for his fourth consecutive start in net for Buffalo against a desperate Boston squad riding Game 5 momentum and home-ice edge, boasting a 95% penalty kill through the series.

title: Who will be confirmed as Fed Chair?
description:
This market will resolve according to the next individual formally confirmed as Chair of the Federal Reserve.

Formal confirmation as Chair of the Federal Reserve requires the Senate to confirm a nominee as Chair of the Federal Reserve. Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count. Senate confirmation of a listed individual as a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors will not alone qualify.

If no Senate confirmation for the position of Chair of the Federal Reserve has occurred by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from the U.S. Senate; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's January nomination of former Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed Chair—whose term expires mid-May—has advanced decisively, driving trader consensus to a 99.6% implied probability on his confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee approved Warsh on a 13-11 party-line vote April 29, overcoming Democratic opposition led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, with Pennsylvania Democrat John Fetterman signaling support. Republicans' Senate majority positions Warsh for swift full-Senate confirmation via simple majority vote, reflecting historical patterns for such nominees amid low controversy. Realistic challenges include unexpected procedural holds, bipartisan defections, late-breaking scandals, or White House withdrawal, though none appear imminent.

title: Brazil Presidential Election
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

The race remains tightly contested due to entrenched polarization between PT and PL bases, Flávio's inheritance of his father's loyal support despite Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility, and a fragmented center-right field splitting votes among Zema, Caiado, and others. Separation could arise from party nominations, economic indicators, gubernatorial endorsements, or scandals ahead of the potential October 25 runoff.

title: Will the Iranian regime fall by May 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a 97.2% "No" probability for the Iranian regime falling by May 31, driven by its demonstrated resilience amid severe economic pressures from the U.S.-led oil blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and earlier 2026 protests sparked by currency collapse and inflation exceeding 70%. U.S. intelligence assessments in March confirmed the leadership remains intact with no imminent collapse risk, as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has effectively suppressed unrest through executions and crackdowns following January-February demonstrations. Recent April cease-fire reports and regime survival post-airstrikes underscore stability, with no mass defections or uprisings in the past 30 days. Realistic shifts could stem from IRGC mutiny, Supreme Leader health crisis, or escalated military action, though the one-month timeline poses significant barriers.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Jordan Bardella at 22.5% and Édouard Philippe at 21.5% for the 2027 French presidential election, mirroring recent polls where Bardella leads first-round voting intentions at 34-38% while Philippe trails at 18-26% in a fragmented field of over 30 candidates. March 2026 municipal elections bolstered Bardella's Rassemblement National with wins in 66 mid-sized communes amid low turnout signaling protest potential, yet the left retained Paris, Marseille, and Lyon, and Philippe's reelection as Le Havre mayor enhanced his anti-far-right appeal. Late-March Elabe and Odoxa polls show Philippe edging Bardella 51-49% in a runoff, sustaining the tight race under France's two-round system. Separation could arise from Marine Le Pen's summer appeal on her election ban, party nominations, or economic shifts fueling immigration discontent.

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding US-Iranian relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count. 

The meeting must be in-person and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid heightened U.S.-Iran tensions from a recent conflict involving a Strait of Hormuz blockade and ceasefire, trader sentiment hinges on stalled direct diplomacy following high-level talks in Islamabad in mid-April, where U.S. Vice President JD Vance and Iranian officials met without agreement. Iran's April 28 proposal for a phased deal—reopening Hormuz first, deferring nuclear talks—remains under White House review, but Tehran's Foreign Minister ruled out direct meetings during his late-April Pakistan visit. President Trump faces a looming 60-day congressional authorization deadline, with mediators pressing for breakthroughs; escalation risks or late diplomatic signals could sway outcomes before any resolution date.
